title: Frozen-release retention screening, 2026-10-15 (retired development corpus)
evidence_class: Six small AI-authored cases fixed privately before comparison of frozen releases, then opened for algorithm development and permanently retired from held-out scoring. Not human-authored, consented real-trace, or representative production evidence.

protocol.counter: ceil(len(json.dumps(messages))/4), Python default JSON encoding. This is a caller-owned estimate, not a provider tokenizer.
source_formats_and_behaviors: semantic questions with little lexical overlap
protocol.retention: An exact required source span must appear in a decoded quoted excerpt or in a retained, unchanged original message. Partial identifiers do not count.
protocol.protected_context: Pinned instructions and active user/tool work must remain exact. Required-span packing costs include the standard historical-quote wrapper and protected messages.
protocol.cache_check: One predeclared tool case was evaluated at 18, 19, and 20 completed cycles. The earlier complete output must be an unchanged prefix of the next output. Two adjacent comparisons are reported separately from six-case retention totals.
protocol.failure_policy: All cases remain in the denominator. Exceptions and unsupported cases would remain reported. Budgets and required spans were not changed after scoring.
protocol.inference: No model or provider calls. No algorithm changes or tuning during this comparison.

interpretation: The frozen 0.10.0 release improved exact retention on this screening but still omitted six of fourteen required spans and failed complete retention on three of six cases, despite feasible budgets. This does not establish mature or general retention quality. Report separately from the earlier fourteen-of-fourteen development result, which used a different, previously disclosed three-case corpus.
reproducibility: The exact frozen input and initial per-case results are now published at benchmarks/retired_frozen_release_screening_2026-10-15.json and docs/results/frozen-release-screening-details-2026-10-15.json. Their SHA256 values match the precomparison declaration above. The files' historical 'private holdout' status describes original creation only; after opening them for development, they cannot serve as unseen validation again. Replaying these files does not reproduce stochastic agent outputs and does not turn this small synthetic corpus into representative task evidence.
